gloss: to pay; to expend; to invest (energy or time)
note: To give your time and effort as something that costs you. When you say 我付出了那么多, you're keeping a quiet tally and feeling that something is owed back.
The world of traditional Chinese opera, named after a Tang emperor's troupe in a pear garden. You hear old stages, painted faces and performers trained from childhood.
To talk something through until both sides understand each other. At work, 我们沟通一下 can sound friendly, and you may also hear a polite warning that something needs sorting out.
Quick and frank, with no fuss or haggling. When someone agrees 爽快, you feel the relief of not having to ask twice.

gloss: benefit (provided by an employer or organization)
note: The perks an employer gives beyond pay, like insurance, meals and holiday gift boxes. You ask about 福利 when weighing a job, and a company's mooncakes at Mid-Autumn count too.
A manager, though the title is handed out freely in China. When a 客户经理 calls you, you assume a salesperson, and they may manage nobody at all.
Your pride, and how easily it bruises. Saying someone's 自尊心强 usually means they can't bear being looked down on, not that they feel good about themselves.
Undisciplined and unwilling to follow the rules. You hear a teacher or a boss writing you up, so it's a criticism and never praise for a free spirit.

gloss: responsible; predisposed to do the right thing; considerate of others
note: Doing the right thing with nobody watching. You see signs saying 请自觉排队, and you feel the public expectation that you should police yourself.

gloss: gratifying (esp. to see sb get their comeuppance)
note: Satisfying because someone finally got what they deserved. You feel pent-up anger drain away, as if you had let out a long breath.

gloss: (after a verb) a bit; a little (indicating brief duration, or softening the tone, or suggesting giving sth a try)
note: Just briefly, a little, added after a verb to soften it. When you say 帮我看一下, you make your request feel small and easy to say yes to.
After all, pointing at the fact that should settle things. When you say 他毕竟是孩子, you're making allowances, and there's often a small sigh in it.
